_comment: YOUR requirements. Shipped as an example: backend/platform SWE in India, 0-3 years asked, >= 20 LPA, Java-leaning stack. Edit title include/exclude, max_min_years, min_pay_lpa, max_age_days, stack weights, gaps and exclude_companies (add your current employer here). Regexes are matched case-insensitively against lower-cased text.

title._comment: Eligibility first (user, 15 Nov 2026): keep EVERY software-development role at the user's level, whatever its stack or domain (frontend, mobile, embedded, ML, platform developers like Salesforce/SAP); the user filters by stack. Out: seniority/intern/contract, and work that isn't development: SRE/DevOps, data engineering, data science, ops/admin/support, sales, QA/test, chip/hardware design. 'exclude' always applies; 'exclude_domain' (support, hardware design) unless a core_override marker; 'include' = core titles; 'exclude_unless_core' drops non-core titles naming non-development work; other titles need an enabled family and the JD check.

title._comment_families: Order matters: a title in a disabled family stays out even if 'generic' would match it. OFF: infra (SRE/DevOps/cloud ops) and data (data engineering): the user doesn't want these. ON: ai (AI/LLM engineer) and generic (titles with no role word); both must pass the JD check. FDE and MTS are core titles. Recall first (15 Nov 2026): never drop a possible software-development role; a few extra wrong ones are acceptable.

software_jd._comment: Counts distinct DEVELOPMENT terms (languages, frameworks, APIs, services, code quality), not ops tooling (Kubernetes, Terraform, Linux, cloud consoles), which ops roles list too. Minus hardware_weight per distinct hardware, plant, ops-admin or support term; must reach min_signals for non-core titles. MTS / Programmer Analyst (jd_check_titles) are rejected only when those penalty terms win. Lenient check: rejected only when penalty terms outnumber software terms.

linkedin._comment: Light mode (default) is India-wide role searches plus a small company sweep: ~5-15 min, and where nearly all LinkedIn-only results come from. --deep adds per-city searches and a big sweep (hours).
linkedin._comment_checkpoint: LinkedIn progress is also saved every checkpoint_seconds between searches; re-running the same day resumes the company sweep with companies not yet searched today.
linkedin._comment_liveness: Earlier LinkedIn postings not seen again are checked on LinkedIn (up to liveness_checks_per_run per pass, rechecked after liveness_recheck_days): closed ones are dropped, open ones kept at any age.

_comment_experience: Roles asking up to max_min_years are kept; 0-2 years with salary evidence is flagged as the sweet spot. Campus, new-grad and fresher hiring is excluded (title and description).
_comment_score_weights: Points per part of the 0-100 score. Pay and level fit come first (prerequisites); stack weighs less than company quality because a stack can be learned, and less than the gap between Strong and Likely pay evidence.
